new.n: Bank-robbery tin box in the Franklin House cellar, North Lansing
new.pl: Franklin House hotel, 414 Franklin St E (now E Cesar E. Chavez Ave), SW corner of Center St, North Lansing (1898 Sanborn sheet 21)
new.v: $60,000 bank-robbery money in a tin box (claimed)
new.st: In 1885 a dying life-term convict at Jackson prison told an ex-sheriff that two lifers, jailed for a $60,000 bank robbery in which the cashier was killed some 30 years earlier, had buried the money in a tin box in the south cellar of the Franklin House. In April 1896 the ex-sheriff and a partner, with the owner's permission and a map, dug a pit 30 ft square and 4 ft deep under the south end of the hotel's Center St wing: no box, but the earth looked recently disturbed. The robbery itself is unverified. Urban lot: look-only.
src: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Lansing, 1898, sheet 21 (Library of Congress)
pinev: Hotel footprint on the 1898 Sanborn sheet 21 at the SW corner of Franklin and Center Streets (about 60 m).
